question.text:
Consider a system with:

  • $6$-level page tables
  • $1$ KB page tables at each level
  • $4$-byte page-table entries

How much page-table space, in KB, is required to allow a process to access two distinct pages whose virtual addresses differ only in their most significant bit?
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider a machine with:

  • Physical memory $=8$ GB
  • Page size $=8$ KB
  • Page-table entry size $=4$ bytes
  • Virtual address size $=46$ bits
  • Every page table must fit into one page

How much physical memory is needed for a process with three pages of virtual memory, for example, one code page, one data page, and one stack page?

Give your answer in KB.
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider a virtual-memory system that uses multi-level paging.

  • Virtual address size $=64$ bits
  • Physical address size $=64$ bits
  • Page size $=1$ MB $=2^{20}$ bytes
  • Page-table entry size $=16$ bytes $=2^4$ bytes
  • Each individual page table at every level must fit in one frame

A particular process uses only $128$ MB $=2^{27}$ bytes of virtual memory, occupying the consecutive virtual-address range:

$0$ to $2^{27}-1$

What is the total number of individual page tables required to translate this process's address space?
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider the $\text{x86-64}$ architecture.

Assume:

  • Pages are $4$ KB
     
  • Each page-table entry is $8$ bytes
     
  • Each page-table page contains $512$ entries
     
  • The page-table structure has four levels
     
  • Any allocated memory consumes physical pages in RAM
     
  • There is no swapping or demand paging

What is the minimum number of physical pages consumed by a process that allocates $12$ KB, for example, one page each for code, stack, and data?
question.subject: Operating System

question.text:
Consider a three-level page table on a system where:

  • Page size $=256$ bytes
  • Page-table entry size $=2$ bytes
  • First-level page tables contain $16$ entries
  • Second-level page tables contain $128$ entries
  • Third-level page tables contain $128$ entries

If the page containing address $\texttt{0x100}$ and the page containing address $\texttt{0x10000}$ are valid for a process, and no other pages are valid, how many bytes of space do the page tables for this process occupy?
question.subject: Operating System
